title: SourceSnapshot@1 payload
description: Immutable identification of source CONTENT, never a branch. The snapshot's own identity is the envelope content_id; branch and PR labels originate as Review Selector inputs and carry no authority. Capture and materialization run offline through sanitized plumbing, so configuration cannot change content identity.

repository_id.description: Stable identity of the repository this content came from, independent of clone path or remote URL.

vcs.description: Backing version-control system. The first adapter is Git-only; core contracts carry no branch commands or PR-provider types.

content_digest.description: Digest over the canonical ordered manifest of included content. Two captures of identical content agree here regardless of host or repository configuration.

parent_snapshot_id.description: Present when this snapshot was DERIVED, e.g. S1 produced by integrating a validated patch into S0. An accepted patch never mutates its base.

source_revision.description: Upstream revision this content corresponds to (a Git commit ID), when one exists. Absent for a synthetic worktree capture. Metadata for humans and provenance — not identity.

artifact_manifest.description: Content object holding the ordered path/mode/identity/digest manifest. Kept out of the event stream by reference.

capture.description: How the content was admitted. A best-effort copy is deliberately NOT a capture kind: it may serve as untrusted diagnostic input, but it can never create a target eligible for convergence or automatic integration.

boundary.description: Which atomic read boundary admitted the dirty tree. `revalidated` means monitoring started before the first read and two complete manifests plus the index digest matched with no intervening or overflowed change event.

attempts.description: Capture attempts consumed before admission. Bounded; exhausting the bound fails closed rather than admitting a torn tree.

included.description: Whether the submodule's content is part of this snapshot. Implicit recursion is disabled during capture, so this is always an explicit policy outcome.
